judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition sweeps in "any and all services provided by Licensee in connection with or relating to the operation" of the facilities, and the phrase "relating to" has no discernible outer boundary — hotel spa, concert, restaurant and off-site services could all qualify or not. That open-ended relational language is the kind of term parties fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its breadth sits against 2(b)(ii)'s restaurant prohibition and 4(a)'s quality standard, which are framed for a narrower band of services, so the reach of "Licensed Services" affects what Licensor may police. No square contradiction appears, but the fit is loose enough to leave some relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is of an "exclusive license" "only in the Morton Territories" and "solely in connection with" development and promotion of Hard Rock Hotel/Casinos, with a worldwide promotion carve-out that excludes "the sale of merchandise" — the interplay of "exclusive," "solely," and the carve-out invites competing readings of what Licensee may do and what Licensor is excluded from. The warranty tail ("subject only to whatever actions or inactions may have been taken or not taken by Morton") is itself indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly made subject to clause 3(a), which reserves to Licensor the right to use the Hard Rock Hotel Marks "anywhere in the world for a Hotel facility that does not include a Casino" — a reservation hard to square with an "exclusive" license of those same marks inside the Morton Territories. That tension between 2(a) and 3(a) is a genuine whole-instrument problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All rights not specifically granted" reserved, coupled with the Licensor's worldwide hotel-without-casino right and the "directly or indirectly" Nevada carve-out, leaves the boundary between a reserved "Hotel" and a licensed "Hotel/Casino" contestable, particularly given 1(f)'s "same Hard Rock complex/development" language. "Affiliated entity" is also undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2(a)'s grant of an exclusive license within the Morton Territories, this reservation of a worldwide hotel right (except Nevada) creates a direct overlap problem, and 11(a) singles out only the Nevada prohibition for injunctive protection. The relationship between these provisions is precisely what a court would have to reconcile.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 3(a) — Reservation of All Rights Not Specifically Granted

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The standard is "good quality at least as high as the quality of similar goods presently sold" at the Las Vegas property and "equal to and commensurate with" existing products — "commensurate," "similar goods" and the frozen 1996 benchmark are vague measures for a perpetual licence. Whether the benchmark is fixed at the Effective Date or floats is genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with 4(b)-(c) inspection rights and with 5(a), which makes quality-control failures arbitrable, so the scheme is coherent; the only strain is that a perpetual term (9(a)) leaves the 1996 baseline permanently frozen. No direct contradiction is identifiable.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 4(a) — Nature and Quality of Licensed Products and Services

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arbitration trigger is limited to disputes "regarding the failure of Licensee to conform to any provision of quality control," a category whose edges are uncertain when a quality complaint overlaps a use-of-marks or scope complaint; "proscribed" for "prescribed" is a further slip. The mandatory "shall be resolved by binding arbitration" is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 5(d) (everything not specifically identified is excluded from arbitration), 11(a) (court injunctions and specific performance) and 14 (New York courts except as provided in Section 5), so characterising a dispute determines the forum. That allocation is workable but a live source of relational argument.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 5(a) — Arbitration of Quality Control Disputes

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any claims or controversies not specifically identified hereinabove, including but not limited to" validity disputes is a classic catch-all set against enumerated specifics, and what counts as "specifically identified hereinabove" in 5(a) is exactly the contested boundary. The wording therefore carries a real general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5(a) (arbitrable quality disputes), 11(a) (court injunctions) and 14 (New York courts "except as provided in Section 5"); these harmonise on their face but the split turns entirely on the undefined boundary this clause draws. Some relational risk, not a flat conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 5(d) — Exclusion of Validity Disputes from Arbitration

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts" is a notoriously indeterminate standard, and here it is untethered to any specified conduct or expenditure to protect the marks. A single sentence with no metric is squarely the kind of vague term courts construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside 6(d), which gives each party a right (not a duty) to sue at its own cost, and 2(b)(iii)'s separate "best efforts" registration duty on Licensor; a party could argue the general duty enlarges those specific allocations. The tension is modest rather than a contradiction.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 6(a) — Best Efforts to Protect the Marks

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "When practical and appropriate" is an open-ended qualifier that could swallow the obligation, and the display must be "reasonably acceptable to Licensor" even though it is Licensee's facilities being promoted — apparently a mechanical slip for "Licensee." Both features give a court something to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The quarterly table-tent duty is specific and does not collide with any other provision I could find; 8(b) and 8(a)(3) run in the same cooperative direction. Relational risk is low.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 8(a)(1) — Promotional Cooperation, Reference to Other Party's Facilities

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "except that" construction leaves it unclear whether Licensee's web-page right in the Morton Territories is exclusive of Licensor or merely permissive, since Licensor may maintain a page for "other Hard Rock Facilities as they may develop" — a category that by 1(j) includes Hard Rock Hotel/Casinos. That is a genuine two-reading ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against 1(j)'s definition of Hard Rock Facilities and 2(b)(v)'s internet-sales regime, Licensor's web rights over "other Hard Rock Facilities" overlap the Licensee's exclusive territorial rights under 2(a). The overlap is real though capable of harmonisation.
judgments.clause_name: Paragraph 8(b) — Worldwide Web Site Development and Maintenance

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any or all of the rights and licenses granted hereunder" is broad but definite, and the flow-down obligation is stated plainly; the only softness is whether a sublicense of "all" rights amounts to an assignment. That single point is arguable but the drafting is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An unrestricted right to sublicense or franchise all rights sits awkwardly with 9(c)'s first-offer requirement on a sale of "all or substantially all" of Licensee's rights, which a full sublicense could effectively circumvent. That interaction is a plausible relational dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals are descriptive and identify the parties and purpose without operative language; "solely for the purposes of" is limiting but is elaborated in the operative grant. Little to construe on the words alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital's "solely for the purposes of operating and promoting" and selling merchandise "in the Hotel/Casinos or Casinos" runs slightly narrower than 2(b)(v), which allows internet sales outside those premises. A modest recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All other marks and rights of every kind pertaining thereto" and "all confusingly similar names ... and derivations thereof, to the maximum extent permitted by law" is an expansive catch-all whose reach is uncertain, especially where it names "Hard Rock" itself. The express carve-out of Hotel and Casino Marks mitigates but does not eliminate this.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 2(b)(iii) (no use of "any Hard Rock Marks not expressly provided herein") and 6(c)/2(b)(ix), which do permit some "Hard Rock" usages; the definitional overlap between "Hard Rock" as a Hard Rock Mark and its licensed use creates some strain. Not a flat contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition simply incorporates Exhibit A and is otherwise a clear exclusion clause; the only softness is the trailing "except as expressly provided herein." Wording is largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A lists both "Hard Rock Casino" and "Hard Rock Hotel," so the Hotel Marks overlap the Casino Marks defined by Exhibit B — an internal duplication that matters where the two sets are treated differently (e.g. 2(b)(i), 3(a)). That overlap is a real, if minor, incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same structure as 1(b): a straightforward reference to Exhibit B with an express exclusion. Nothing ambiguous in the wording itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B's single entry "Hard Rock Casino" also appears in Exhibit A, so the same mark falls within both definitions, which are given different treatment in 2(b)(i) and 3(a). That duplication invites construction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All-inclusive place for lodging," "indoor corridors" and "a variety of amenities" are vague criteria that could exclude many real hotels and turn on debatable facts. The definition is short but genuinely fuzzy at the edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds 1(f), 1(g) and 3(a)'s reservation of a worldwide right for a "Hotel facility that does not include a Casino," so its boundary allocates rights between the parties. No direct contradiction, but the definition carries weight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such as slot machines, gaming tables and the like" is an enumerated list with a catch-all, and "a substantial source of revenue and its principal function" is a vague dual test. Both features give room for argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with 1(f), 1(h) and 2(b)(ix)'s riverboat provision, which expressly builds on the riverboat sentence here. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Immediately adjoining contiguous facility" and "part of the same 'Hard Rock' complex/development" are imprecise spatial tests with no metric. The second limb in particular has no discernible boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 2(b)(i)'s bar on using Hotel Marks in a non-Hotel/Casino and with 3(a)'s reservation of hotel-only rights, so its boundary determines whether Licensor's reserved right is available nearby. Some tension, no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple compound definition referring to defined terms and the Morton Territories; nothing vague in its own words. It is essentially mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1(f)-(i) and 2(a); the term is scarcely used elsewhere. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional cross-reference with no evaluative language. Definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with 2(a), 2(b)(i) and 2(b)(ix); no inconsistency identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Hard Rock Hotel Marks and/or the Hard Rock Casino Marks" is a routine drafting formula and the rest is cross-referential. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1(f), 2(a) and 2(b)(i). No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed collective definition of three enumerated facility types; there is no catch-all. Wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matters in 8(a)(1), 8(b) and 2(b)(vii), and in 8(b) it arguably lets Licensor build web pages for facilities licensed exclusively to Licensee. That downstream effect is a modest relational point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The territory is defined with precision by state, river, radius and named nations; the typo "radius form" and "(SO)" for (50) do not change meaning. Illinois is expressly included despite lying east of the Mississippi, so no inconsistency arises.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(a), 3(a) and 8(a)(1), all of which turn on this definition without contradicting it. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any and all personal property, products and merchandise bearing" the marks is broad but self-executing; the categories overlap rather than conflict. Little genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 6(c), which says Licensee "shall not use, sell or display any merchandise bearing such designations," there is a question whether merchandise bearing designation-style marks is a Licensed Product. Some tension, largely resolved by 2(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain identification of the entity plus successors and assigns. Nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12 gives the Licensor's notice address as Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc., a different entity from Rank Licensing, Inc., and 3(a) refers to "affiliated entities" not covered by this definition. A minor mismatch worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two crisp sentences: no Hotel Marks except in a Hotel/Casino, but Casino Marks may be used in a standalone Casino. The only softness comes from the incorporated 1(f) definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(a) and 3(a)'s mirror-image reservation of hotel-only rights to Licensor. No conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The syntax leaves it unclear whether "that is confusingly similar to a Hard Rock Cafe restaurant" qualifies every restaurant or only those "anywhere else," and "confusingly similar" and "other types of restaurants" are themselves elastic. That modifier placement is a real construction problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The second sentence permitting "other types of restaurants" partially cures the first, and 1(a)'s broad Hard Rock Marks definition keeps cafe rights with Licensor; the pieces harmonise with effort. Moderate but not acute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Best efforts to maintain, protect and preserve" and "reasonably likely to affect" are soft standards, but the operative sequence (Licensor files; on failure Licensee may file as agent) is clear. Middling on wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13 expressly carves this clause out of the no-agency rule, and 6(b) bars Licensee registrations — the two are reconciled by the express cross-reference. Fit is good.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Contiguous to" a Hard Rock Hotel/Casino and the absolute "Licensed Products must always bear the geographic location where sold" are firm-sounding but their application to designation merchandise and internet sales is uncertain. Some ambiguity in "contiguous."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly subject to 2(b)(v) (internet) and 2(b)(vii), and its "always bear the geographic location" rule must be read with 2(b)(vi)'s permission to substitute "Beach Club" designations inside the facility. The cross-references mostly reconcile them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rule that internet-designated goods may not be sold in retail stores and vice versa is clear, though "Hard Rock Internet access kits" is an undefined product category. Mostly definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express exception to 2(b)(iv)'s mail-order and geographic-marking rules, and the recital contemplates merchandise sold "in the Hotel/Casinos or Casinos" only. The recital tension is slight but present.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The other designations such as 'Beach Club' or 'Athletic Club'" is an illustrative list introduced by "such as," leaving the class of permitted substitute designations undefined. That is a genuine list-scope problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibits D and E, invoked by 2(b)(vii) and (viii), both contain the very same "Beach Club/Athletic Club" designations under inconsistent regimes, which unsettles this clause's permission. That overlap is a concrete relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is temporally precise (eighteen months) and the two sentences separate designation use from merchandise sales. Wording itself is reasonably clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D and Exhibit E list identical designations ("Beach Club"/"Athletic Club"), yet this clause permits their continued use in other Hard Rock Hotels while 2(b)(viii) requires that Licensee "forever cease displaying such designations" after eighteen months. That is a direct contradiction on the face of the two exhibits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Whatever merchandise is currently being sold" is imprecise as a defined universe, and "forever cease displaying such designations" is stark but clear. Moderate wording risk from the undefined merchandise set.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Exhibit E duplicates Exhibit D, this permanent cessation obligation collides with 2(b)(vii)'s permission to carry the same designations into other Hard Rock Hotels. The two subsections cannot both be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Certain terminology, such as 'Riverboat'" is illustrative, and "legally required terminology" depends on a jurisdiction's rules, but the mechanism (use within the circle logo, request registration) is definite. Mild list-scope softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with 1(e)'s inclusion of riverboats and with 2(b)(iii)'s registration procedure, which it expressly invokes. No inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Never to attack or assist another in attacking" is broad but its meaning is plain, and "the Term of this Agreement or thereafter" is clear given the perpetual term. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5(d) contemplates that validity disputes may be litigated in court, which sits oddly with an absolute no-challenge covenant; 16's survivability supports the "thereafter" language. Modest tension with 5(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard goodwill-inurement acknowledgment with no evaluative or open-ended term. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3(a), 3(b) and the definitions, which all keep ownership with Licensor. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Dominate, modify or qualify" is a vague triad and the carve-out is only for "geographical designations," leaving unclear what other additions are barred. Real but contained ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause 2(b)(vi) expressly allows substituting "Beach Club" or "Athletic Club" for the geographic designation, which is not a geographical designation and therefore appears to fall outside this clause's carve-out. That is a specific tension between 3(d) and 2(b)(vi).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, closed catch-all tying use to the Agreement's provisions with a written-consent escape. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(a), 2(b) and 23's amendment requirement. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable access," "reasonable notice" and "will not cause any disruption" are soft, and the last phrase is arguably absolute in a way that could defeat inspection. Some wording softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pairs with 4(c), 4(f) and 5(a) coherently as a quality-control scheme. No inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is syntactically awkward ("furnish or render ... requested Licensed Services, representative samples on the premises of each Licensed Product"), but the sense is recoverable. Mild mechanical roughness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates within the 4(b) inspection framework and does not cut against any other provision. Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blanket compliance covenant in plain terms; "in all respects" is broad but not ambiguous. Low risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 2(b)(ix)'s accommodation of jurisdictional gaming terminology; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Wherever the same may be used with reasonable convenience" is a vague trigger, and "the appropriate notice of registration" assumes registrations that may not exist. Both invite argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Registration is controlled by Licensor under 2(b)(iii), so the notice obligation depends on Licensor's own filings; that dependency is workable but not spelled out. Slight relational looseness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purpose acknowledgment, declaratory in form, with the single word "solely" doing the work. Little scope for dispute on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It echoes Section 13's final sentence and constrains 4(b) inspection rights consistently. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any and all remedies and relief whatsoever that is deemed appropriate" is expansive but expressly illustrated; the grammar slip ("that is") does not change meaning. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Arbitral power to grant permanent injunctions overlaps 11(a)'s grant of court injunctive relief and 14's forum clause, raising a question of which forum enjoins what. A real but resolvable overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise timing and enforceability provision with a defined law and forum for entry of judgment. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5(a), 5(d) and 14's New York choice of law. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition is broad ("nor take any action itself which would affect the ownership of or damage, dilute or modify") but the conduct barred is identifiable. Some breadth, little genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause 2(b)(iii) expressly contemplates Licensee preparing and filing registration documents as Licensor's agent, and 2(b)(ix) requires Licensee to request riverboat registrations; the absolute language here must yield to those. A discernible tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence permits designation use but bars "any merchandise bearing such designations," while the first bars any confusingly similar designation at all — the interaction of the absolute bar and the 2(b) exception is not clean. "Such designations" has an uncertain referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The flat merchandise bar contradicts 2(b)(vii) and (viii), which expressly allow designation-bearing merchandise to be sold for eighteen months, and sits against 1(m)'s Licensed Products definition. That is a specific inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Each party may sue "at its own cost" and keep recoveries, yet "Licensor will always have full control of any joint proceedings" with costs and recoveries shared equally — the boundary between individual and "joint" proceedings is undefined. That gap is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 6(a)'s best-efforts duty and 11(a)'s injunctive remedies without contradiction, though it allocates enforcement differently from the mutual best-efforts pledge. Fit is broadly coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-way indemnity covering "any suits, loss and damage arising out of any service or act" performed "in connection with this Agreement, or in relation to" the marks — "in relation to" is very broad and its outer limit unstated. One-sided breadth increases construction risk against the drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No reciprocal indemnity or limitation appears elsewhere, and 2(a)'s ownership warranty by Licensor is not carved out of this indemnity. That omission is a minor incoherence at most.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete, factually specific obligation about book credits with dates and named roles. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of Section 8's cooperation scheme; no other provision touches it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Same size and style" is a clear enough parity requirement, triggered only by maps identifying "all locations." Minor softness in the trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8(a)(1) and 8(b) cooperation obligations. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement merely "to discuss the possibility" of sponsorship imposes no ascertainable obligation, which is itself the kind of indefiniteness a court would have to address. But its very toothlessness makes disputes unlikely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably within the Section 8 cooperation provisions and contradicts nothing. Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "A license granted in perpetuity" is short and unequivocal on its face. There is no ambiguity in the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16 speaks of provisions surviving "the termination of this Agreement" and 5(a) contemplates cure of quality failures, yet no termination right exists anywhere — a perpetual, unterminable licence with survivability language is an internal oddity. That mismatch is worth flagging.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Royalty free and fully paid" with sole entitlement to economic benefits is plain and unqualified. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the absence of any payment machinery elsewhere; the only friction is 6(d)'s equal division of joint recoveries, which is a different subject. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All or substantially all of his assets and/or rights," "negotiate in good faith" and the re-triggering condition ("if Licensee again initiates a Transfer Proposal") are each imprecise, and the six-month sentence's operation is not clear. Several soft terms in one clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10 permits unrestricted sublicensing or franchising of all rights, which could achieve a transfer without triggering this first-offer duty, and 18 binds transferees generally. That interaction is a plausible dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is detailed and even-handed on the Nevada point, with defined consequences ("without bond") and a savings sentence. Little textual ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Court injunctive relief here overlaps the arbitrator's injunctive powers under 5(b) and the arbitration mandate in 5(a) for quality disputes. A recognisable forum overlap rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional non-waiver clause in standard terms. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Section 22's written-waiver requirement without contradiction. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Delivery methods and deemed-receipt rules are stated with reasonable precision, though no deemed time is given for air courier separately from hand delivery. Minor gap only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Licensor's notice address is Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc., not Rank Licensing, Inc. as defined in 1(n) and the preamble — a mismatch between the notice block and the contracting party. Worth some relational weight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The no-agency and no-joint-venture language is standard and its one exception is expressly cross-referenced. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The express carve-out for 2(b)(iii) shows the drafters harmonised it with the agency filing right; nothing else conflicts. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Choice of New York substantive law and New York courts, with an express carve-out for Section 5, is clear on its face. "Arising out of or relating to" is broad but its function here is unremarkable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5(a) sites arbitration alternately in California and New York, and 5(d) sends non-quality claims to "a court of competent jurisdiction," which this clause narrows to New York; the pieces mostly cohere. Slight friction only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate severability clause with conventional wording. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the whole instrument; no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Which, in order to be effective, or by its nature, must survive" is a soft self-selecting test, leaving which covenants survive undetermined. Mild vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause presupposes a termination, yet 9(a) grants a perpetual licence and no termination right exists anywhere in the Agreement. That mismatch is a genuine coherence question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to "the Purchase and Sale Agreement" without defining or dating it, and extinguishes rights under named prior settlements "including but not limited to the License Agreements" — an undefined capitalised term inside a catch-all. Both features create textual uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause makes an undefined external document part of the entire agreement, which bears on 2(a)'s grant and 3(a)'s reservation; whether prior Morton rights survive is exactly what the extinguishment sentence addresses. Some relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard successors-and-assigns clause; "as the case may be" is filler rather than ambiguity. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Binding transferees generally sits alongside 9(c)'s first-offer restriction and 10's sublicense flow-down without contradicting them. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, plain corporate authority representation. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 20 and 21; no conflict. Note there is no matching Licensee authority representation, but that is an omission rather than an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard enforceability representation with a customary bankruptcy/equity qualifier; the stray comma after "constitutes" changes nothing. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "all of the Parties hereto," a term not capital-defined but obvious from the preamble; nothing contradicts it. Consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision uses "the Morton Parties" and "the Rank Parties," neither of which is defined anywhere in this Agreement, and the enumerated list ends in "or other commitment" as a catch-all. The undefined party terms are a mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble and 1(n) define only "Licensor" and "Licensee," so these imported terms appear carried over from the related Purchase and Sale Agreement referenced in Section 17. That cross-document mismatch is a real coherence point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional written-waiver requirement with a clear formality. Nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 11(b)'s non-waiver language and 23's amendment formality. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The inclusion of "or interpreted" among the acts requiring a written instrument is unusual and arguably purports to control construction itself. That word is a small oddity but unlikely to be litigated alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17 also states the Agreement "cannot be modified except by a written instrument signed by the parties," so the two are duplicative rather than conflicting. Consistent.
